title: Faithfulness vs. Plausibility: On the (Un)Reliability of Explanations from Large Language Models
method: Conceptual review distinguishing plausibility and model faithfulness, covering token importance, counterfactuals and CoT; application-specific transparency discussion.
evaluation: Illustrative examples and synthesis of prior studies; not a new controlled benchmark or measured improvement.
limitations: Conceptual definitions and recommendations do not certify a method; domain examples do not establish empirical deployment outcomes.
claim_preservation_overlap: Already argues for meeting both user-facing and model-facing needs; no specified typed decision-evidence preservation experiment across audience rewrites in inspected text.
novelty_implication: Motivation is established; do not claim invention of the plausibility-faithfulness distinction.
baseline_feasibility: Conceptual foundation rather than executable baseline.
corrections_to_interim: Primary source now read, replacing secondary citation only.

title: Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
method: Intervenes on generated CoT by early answering, mistakes, filler tokens and paraphrasing; measures subsequent answers. Main experiments use a175B RLHF model; model-size experiments are separate.
evaluation: Eight multiple-choice tasks;100reasoning samples/problem, temperature0.8 and nucleus p0.95. Task-dependent effects; paraphrase experiment isolates phrasing by hiding the original question from the paraphraser and preserving a later continuation.
limitations: §5 explicitly lacks independent access to true internal reasoning. No guarantee that behavioral robustness establishes complete faithfulness. Proprietary models and sampling cost limit direct reproduction.
claim_preservation_overlap: Paraphrase intervention is existing prior art; not audience-specific rendering of a fixed decision/evidence record.
novelty_implication: Do not claim novel paraphrase robustness or first behavioral intervention tests.
baseline_feasibility: Use its controlled-intervention logic; repeating175B/100samples is not required for a bounded thesis pilot.
corrections_to_interim: Primary source now read; conclusions are conditional on tasks/models, not universal unfaithfulness.

title: Verification and Refinement of Natural Language Explanations through LLM-Symbolic Theorem Proving
method: Explanation-Refiner converts NLI premises, hypotheses and explanatory facts into Isabelle/HOL theories using event semantics/FOL, corrects syntax, proposes proof steps, and refines explanations using failed proof feedback.
evaluation: Evaluates formalized entailment and refinement on e-SNLI,QASC,WorldTree with open/closed LLMs; measures logical validity and autoformalization errors.
limitations: Guarantees concern the formalized theory under its assumptions; natural-language-to-logic translation can lose semantics. Logical support is distinct from tracing an unchanged LLM decision. Authors caution that safety/correctness guarantees in critical applications require further investigation.
claim_preservation_overlap: Formal external checks, sentence-level semantic preservation and refinement already exist. Not an inspected multi-audience preservation protocol tied to target-LLM attributions and behavioralCF outcomes.
novelty_implication: Formalizing claims or adding an external checker alone is not new; this is important direct prior art.
baseline_feasibility: Architecture comparator; full reproduction adds Isabelle, formalization prompts and iterative model calls.
corrections_to_interim: New full-text predecessor; narrows generic external-verification novelty.
